headline_marked: Tarique Rahman [[detained and tortured at JIC]] during 1/11 period, says ICT prosecutor
headline: Tarique Rahman detained and tortured at JIC during 1/11 period, says ICT prosecutor
summary: ICT Chief Prosecutor Md Aminul Islam revealed the details during an inspection of the Joint Interrogation Cell (JIC) at DGFI headquarters.
details: International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) Chief Prosecutor Md Aminul Islam stated that Tarique Rahman was detained and tortured at the Joint Interrogation Cell (JIC) during the military-backed caretaker government in the 1/11 period.
The revelation came after an inspection of the JIC, an alleged secret detention facility located at the DGFI headquarters in Dhaka.
The inspection was conducted by tribunal judges, prosecution, and defence lawyers to investigate claims of prolonged detention and torture of victims of enforced disappearance.
Two crimes against humanity cases involving enforced disappearances are currently being tried before the tribunal against former prime minister Sheikh Hasina and several army officers.
The prosecution has identified other alleged secret detention facilities, including one at Kochukhet and another at the headquarters of Rab-1 in Uttara.
The tribunal judges had previously visited the 'Aynaghar' (House of Mirrors) at the Rab-1 headquarters on August 1.

Chief Prosecutor Aminul Islam argued that such site visits are necessary for a fair adjudication of the cases, citing similar practices in international tribunals for Rwanda and the former Yugoslavia.
caption:
Tarique Rahman was tortured at the JIC during the 1/11 period, according to the ICT Chief Prosecutor.

International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) Chief Prosecutor Md Aminul Islam stated that Tarique Rahman was detained and tortured at the Joint Interrogation Cell (JIC) during the military-backed caretaker government in the 1/11 period.

The revelation came after an inspection of the JIC, an alleged secret detention facility located at the DGFI headquarters in Dhaka.

The inspection was conducted by tribunal judges, prosecution, and defence lawyers to investigate claims of prolonged detention and torture of victims of enforced disappearance.

Two crimes against humanity cases involving enforced disappearances are currently being tried before the tribunal against former prime minister Sheikh Hasina and several army officers.

The prosecution has identified other alleged secret detention facilities, including one at Kochukhet and another at the headquarters of Rab-1 in Uttara.

The tribunal judges had previously visited the 'Aynaghar' (House of Mirrors) at the Rab-1 headquarters on August 1.

Chief Prosecutor Aminul Islam argued that such site visits are necessary for a fair adjudication of the cases, citing similar practices in international tribunals for Rwanda and the former Yugoslavia.

headline_marked: Bowled out for 54: [[Bangladesh suffer innings defeat]] in warm-up game
headline: Bowled out for 54: Bangladesh suffer innings defeat in warm-up game
summary: The Tigers are bowled out for just 54 in their second innings, falling to an innings-and-38-run loss against Cricket Australia XI in Darwin.
details: Bangladesh suffered a crushing innings-and-38-run defeat against Cricket Australia XI in a three-day warm-up match in Darwin, just days before their Test series against Australia.
The batting collapse was severe in the second innings, where the visitors were bowled out for only 54 runs. They added just 35 runs to their overnight score of 19 for two.
Tanzid Tamim top-scored with 22 off 41 balls. No other batter reached double figures, with Shadman Islam, Mominul Haque, and Mehidy Hasan Miraz all scoring just six runs each.
The destruction was led by rookie pacer Campbell Thompson, who tore through the Tigers' lineup to take 8 wickets for 25 runs in 11 overs.
Despite the heavy loss, there was a positive update on Taijul Islam. National team physio Bayjedul Islam confirmed that the spinner's finger injury has improved significantly.
The physio expressed confidence that Taijul will be fit and available for the first Test match, which begins in Darwin on August 13.
caption:
Bowled out for 54! 🏏

Bangladesh suffers a crushing innings defeat in their final warm-up before the Test series.

Bangladesh suffered a crushing innings-and-38-run defeat against Cricket Australia XI in a three-day warm-up match in Darwin, just days before their Test series against Australia.

The batting collapse was severe in the second innings, where the visitors were bowled out for only 54 runs. They added just 35 runs to their overnight score of 19 for two.

Tanzid Tamim top-scored with 22 off 41 balls. No other batter reached double figures, with Shadman Islam, Mominul Haque, and Mehidy Hasan Miraz all scoring just six runs each.

The destruction was led by rookie pacer Campbell Thompson, who tore through the Tigers' lineup to take 8 wickets for 25 runs in 11 overs.

Despite the heavy loss, there was a positive update on Taijul Islam. National team physio Bayjedul Islam confirmed that the spinner's finger injury has improved significantly.

The physio expressed confidence that Taijul will be fit and available for the first Test match, which begins in Darwin on August 13.
